core.title: Keep every wagon's features manifest listing every feature module with its current status
core.given: Any wagon and its features manifest (the wagon's index of its feature modules and their statuses; its concrete name and location come from the profile)
core.when: The planner authors, updates or relies on that wagon's plan artifacts, or finds the manifest out of step with the wagon's feature modules
core.then: The wagon's features manifest lists every feature module of the wagon together with its current status.
prefer: Update the features manifest in the same change that adds, removes, renames or re-statuses a feature module.
Treat the features manifest as the wagon's single index of feature modules and statuses.
Correct an existing omission or stale status when you encounter it, even if your triggering edit was elsewhere.
avoid: Feature modules that exist under the wagon but are missing from the features manifest.
Entries whose status is stale or no longer matches the feature's actual state.
Entries for feature modules that no longer exist.
core.why: The features manifest is the wagon's index of its feature modules and statuses; feature registration and wagon-feature coverage checks read it, so an incomplete or stale manifest breaks them.
evidence: Every feature module under the wagon has a matching entry in its features manifest, and every entry corresponds to an existing feature module.
Each entry carries a status that reflects the feature's current state.
verification: Scope is per wagon and unconditional: a check compares each wagon's feature modules and their actual states with that wagon's features manifest, regardless of which edit surfaced the mismatch.
Severity 2, disposition documentation-only: a manifest mismatch is reported as documentation and is not enforced as a failure.

The change triggers (feature added, removed, renamed, status changed) and the manifest comparison need diff-level observers that do not exist yet; this rule's detector and finding identifiers are realization details.
Identifying wagons, feature modules and the features manifest inside the repository is structure-profile data; the check itself hard-codes no paths, names or suffixes.

values: wagon features manifest omits an existing feature module
wagon features manifest entry carries a stale status

fires: Any wagon exists whose features manifest omits one of its feature modules or carries a status that is not current, regardless of what edit surfaced it.
A planner adds, removes, renames or changes the status of a feature module in a wagon.
A planner creates or edits a wagon's features manifest or other wagon plan artifacts.
A planner's work (including edits to feature internals, code or tests) reveals that a wagon's manifest is incomplete or stale.
doesNotFire: Work that concerns no wagon at all (no wagon, feature module or features manifest is involved or affected).

profileRequirements.meaning: The path or name pattern by which the artifact that indexes one wagon's feature modules and their current statuses (the features manifest) is recognized, so the core can name 'the wagon's features manifest' and a check can locate it in each wagon.

proposedKeys.meaning: Path or name pattern of the artifact that indexes one wagon's feature modules and their current statuses (the features manifest), so a rule can name and a check can locate it in each wagon.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: layout.plan_item only addresses plan artifacts under the plan root (e.g. WMBTs), while the features manifest lives inside each wagon; suffix.plan_artifact is one generic list for all plan-artifact kinds and cannot single out the features-manifest artifact that this rule is entirely about.

neutralityNotes: "Wagon", "feature module", "planner" and "plan artifact" are treated as stack-neutral topology concepts already used by the closed vocabulary (layout.wagon_dir, layout.feature_dir, urn.wagon, urn.feature), not as Bun specifics. The features manifest's concrete name and location are stack data: no existing key identifies that artifact, so layout.features_manifest is proposed and its Bun value (**/_features.yaml, from activation.facts[1]) is recorded. bun.json states only that glob, so layout.wagon_dir and layout.feature_dir (which directories are wagons / feature modules) are not listed in profileRequirements even though a realization needs them; their values live in the stack's structure profile, not in this sidecar. The Bun-only fact type "path_glob" was normalized to the closed fact vocabulary as file_kind; the finding ids, the detector-facing term table and the concrete file name remain bunOnly. "Current status" is kept uninterpreted, exactly as the Bun text does (the status vocabulary is not defined there).
